verdict.rationale: iTerm2 ships a built-in LLM chat window. Linked to sessions, it gives context-aware help, runs commands on your behalf and explains output (gh-6), and it also works in browser sessions (gh-16). However, it depends on an optional AI plugin (docs-15) and a user-supplied OpenAI key (comm-1, comm-2), and the evidence only covers running shell commands, not driving iTerm2's own UI (panes, profiles, settings) by natural language. Missing for 10: natural-language control of the app's own features beyond shell commands, in-depth first-party docs on the AI chat's capabilities, hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation, and support that works without an extra plugin or external API key.
